problem: Existing dialog-based VLN benchmarks (e.g., CVDN, Talk the Walk) are simulation-only and rely on unrealistic assumptions, so there is no dataset of human-human dialogs for controlling a physical robot that combines global localization with multi-target navigation.
motivation: Applications such as search-and-rescue and assistive guidance need robots that can localize and navigate through natural language dialog with non-expert users. Simulation-only benchmarks ignore the noise of physical robots and expensive real-world data collection, so a real-robot dialog dataset is needed to develop sample-efficient models.
key_idea: Collect human-human Commander/Driver dialogs guiding a physical rover through tabletop mazes to three object targets, and define Localization-from-Dialog and Navigation-from-Dialog-History tasks, supported by a ray-tracing replay simulator.
insight: Dialogs are long and complex: over 50% need history, about 25% involve mistakes and repair, and about 15% require re-localization. A simple S2S model beats the random and immediate-stop baselines, and student forcing beats teacher forcing on topological distance (3.38 vs 3.76 test). However, the vision-only ablation is not significantly worse than the full model, and SR is about 0, so the benchmark remains very hard and language grounding is weak.
method: Data collection: 16 participants in 41 teams, with a Commander seeing a static top-down map and a Driver seeing the robot camera; they communicate via text chat only, yielding 169 trials over 116 mazes, with a leaderboard scoring time and command penalties.
Dialog analysis: annotated 34 dialogs for phenomena (needs history 53%, communication repair 26.5%, re-localization repair 14.7%, surrender control 11.8%, perceptual differences 2.9%).

Replay simulator: mazes are annotated as occupancy grids (0.07 m spacing), with actions forward/left 45°/right 45°/stop and 13 rays over a 78° FOV (Bresenham ray tracing) returning color, depth and collision flag.

Tasks and metrics: Localization from Dialog (predict robot position on the map from the dialog) and Navigation from Dialog History (predict actions to reach the next object), evaluated by Topological Map Distance (TD) and Oracle Stopping TD.

Baseline S2S model: an LSTM encoder over GloVe-embedded dialog tokens (with <COM>/<DRI> speaker tokens) initializes an LSTM decoder that takes ray observations and predicts actions; trained with teacher or student forcing with cross-entropy loss, with collision actions and early stop masked.

setting.backbone: LSTM encoder-decoder with GloVe-300 embeddings (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: RobotSlang NDH training fold (120 trials, 360 instances; train+val for test evaluation)
setting.observation: simulated 13-ray color/depth/collision readings approximating the front-facing monocular RGB camera, plus dialog text
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: forward 0.07 m, left 45°, right 45°, stop
setting.simulator: custom RobotSlang replay simulator (ray-tracing occupancy grid); data collected on a physical tabletop-maze rover
setting.privileged: none for navigation (collision actions are masked and stop is disallowed until at the destination); human Commander sees the global map

numbers.extra: trained on train+val; replay simulation; 120 max steps

numbers_note: SR/SPL values were printed as fractions (.04 = 4%) and are reproduced as printed. The 'test' split label for the human study is approximate (all LfD instances). Metrics are in meters.
results: Best S2S model (student forcing, vision+language) gets TD 3.38 m on test vs 4.31/4.33 for random and immediate-stop baselines. Humans localize to within 0.446 m. Student forcing significantly outperforms teacher forcing, but success rates are near zero.
limitations: Navigation was evaluated only in the replay simulator; real-robot transfer was not validated due to COVID-19.
The baseline has no memory or history modeling despite over 50% of dialogs requiring it, and no learned model is provided for the localization task.
Small dataset (169 trials), and agents almost never reach the target (SR about 0).
